brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent cells (piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full) each fitted with a solid bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full). Props (fork, spoon, knife) staged inside demonstrate utensil use. Capped and joint-bolted.

Shape helps: selected solid full-depth bins with no drain holes (hex-bin-full) to contain liquids. Actual waterproofness is unmet - configurator checks fit/collisions only; parts are 3D-printed in a user-chosen material and layer sealing/ watertightness is not verified.

Not verified by this system - configurator checks fit and mesh clearance only. It knows nothing about material, heat resistance, food/dishwasher safety or printing process. Choose a suitable material/process outside the configurator; the geometry alone does not guarantee dishwasher safety.

finish.summary: Built a compact 2-cell utensil holder with two solid full-depth bins (no drains) to support waterproof intent, capped and locked. Demonstrated with fork/spoon/knife props. Waterproof can only be partially helped by shape (solid bins) and dishwasher safety cannot be verified here: both depend on user-chosen material/process which the configurator does not check.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
